scope: Two selected Jenny founders-only OpenRouter reruns with three policy safeguards enabled; same inputs, no context restoration; not an overall benchmark
reference_quality: Automated candidate annotations, not human validated; neutral questions and subjective direction labels affect strict direction matching.

cases.decision_justification: Aura is attractive on founder-market fit, execution, and early enterprise traction. Kelsey connects the product to her own debt experience and Goldman Sachs background, while her cofounder is a certified money coach (P-001, P-002, P-015). The company showed resourcefulness by moving from DTC to an ERG-led enterprise wedge, adding 15 paying corporate partners, winning a Fortune 100 rollout, and reporting $830,000 in contracted revenue with more than $100,000 realized this year (P-022, P-023, P-025). Adoption and reported employer-partner retention are also encouraging (P-005, P-008, P-018). The conventional thesis-fit route therefore creates substantial interest, and the unresolved economics, regulatory, and portability questions are ordinary diligence rather than automatic vetoes. However, Aura is raising $3 million on a SAFE at a $15 million post-money valuation, with approximately $1 million remaining for fund participation (P-029, P-030, P-031). Everywhere is described as a small-check, early-stage investor whose valuation discipline follows from limited ownership and follow-on capital; the supplied guidance cites an approximately $10 million pre-seed ceiling and a typical $6–12 million range (W-c888be75a57b2d241517, W-c0023935be3c2b0a128a, W-ccd36f0acc882b44b168). The current price is $5 million, or 50%, above the cited approximate ceiling and $3 million above the cited typical upper end. I also tested the founder-conviction route. Aura's founder quality and commercial traction could justify tolerating incomplete product and unit-economics diligence, but they do not establish a price exception. The closest observed In, Levee, involved strong founder hustle and early commercial promise, but Fielding's interest remained expressly price-sensitive and does not show a comparable commitment at Aura's valuation (H-2fed83df7ab9758f6301, H-3e2571f333750ac32e49). The closest Out, CurieDX, shows that an impressive founder did not overcome financing scale and operating complexity that did not fit the pre-seed model (H-9e235dd7565a1e109316, H-2c005e1293da471d0b44). Accordingly, C7 controls and I predict no concrete pitch-stage commitment.

In. I would make an exploratory small first-check commitment, subject to ordinary verification. The conventional thesis-fit case is sufficient: Finnecto is B2B enterprise software operating across Latin America, fitting Everywhere's cross-category and geography-independent pre-seed mandate (P-005, P-012; W-3590138e576ab001083b, W-a8d214bf3979de09c9e1). The strongest evidence is concrete early execution: 20 enterprise customers across four countries, more than $100,000 ARR, founder-led sales, and four-week integrations (P-004, P-009, P-015, P-017). The founders also identified and corrected a failed purchasing-manager sales hypothesis by shifting toward CFO-led selling (P-018, P-019, P-020). The $1 million raise is directionally compatible with the cited early-stage round range, although the precise check and syndicate structure remain unknown (P-004; W-a686b6c68c40dfc2cc93, W-3590138e576ab001083b). The stated $5 million post-money valuation is below the roughly $10 million pre-seed ceiling and within the cited $6–12 million typical range, with the qualification that the policy evidence refers primarily to pre-seed pricing while the pitch gives a post-money figure (P-024; W-c888be75a57b2d241517, W-c0023935be3c2b0a128a, W-ccd36f0acc882b44b168). This more closely resembles the observed In precedent Levee, where Fielding saw founder hustle and a viable business and was willing to contemplate a small check while leaving technology and price verification open (H-2fed83df7ab9758f6301, H-3e2571f333750ac32e49). The closest Out comparison is CurieDX, where multiple business models, a $4 million pre-seed raise, and an FDA path made the opportunity too complicated despite an impressive founder (H-9e235dd7565a1e109316, H-2c005e1293da471d0b44). Finnecto has a smaller round, a defined current B2B SaaS product, and materially stronger reported enterprise traction. The future transactional model is a diligence risk and possible upside, not the basis of the present commitment.
